title: Personalized Fall Prevention in Older Adults: A Single-Group Pre–Post Feasibility Study of Needs- and Preference-Guided Evidence-Based Training Programs
summary:
Many older adults experience a decline in physical capacity, which can lead to balance problems, falls, injuries, and limitations in daily activities. Preventive programs for older adults at increased risk of falling are scarce. Existing programs are often rigid and insufficiently adaptable to the individual needs of participants, which leads to low uptake and limited long-term use.
The aim of this study is to develop and test a personalized prevention program within a ‘Center for Healthy Aging’ that identifies individual needs and aligns them with the personal preferences of the participants.
As part of an initial assessment, individual risk factors and support needs are evaluated. These results are then discussed with participants to incorporate their personal wishes and preferences. Based on this, each participant receives a tailored training program.
The prevention program combines evidence-based fall prevention training with individual preferences and—depending on participant choice—modern options such as app-based training.
conditions: accidental falls, fall-related injuries, physical function, mobility

interventions.name: Participants first complete a self-screening of their fall risk (digital or print-based), based on the algorithm of the World Falls Guideline/Federal Initiative for Fall Prevention. criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- community-dwelling
- moderate or high fall risk according to the Federal Initiative for Fall Prevention (BIS) algorithm
Exclusion criteria:
- cognitive impairment
- absolute or relative contraindication to physical training
- participation in regular training focused on function, balance, and/or strength
- insufficient German language proficiency
